# ISA 401 — R Code Study Guide

This file is a code-focused reference based on the provided study material. It covers the R code patterns needed for the questions/topics in the material: R objects and indexing, importing data, exploring data, strings, web scraping, robots.txt, APIs/JSON, functions, purrr, tidy data, data types, and visualization/data encoding.

---

# 1. Setup: Packages

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install packages only if you do not already have them:
# install.packages(c(
#   "dplyr", "readr", "jsonlite", "stringr",
#   "rvest", "robotstxt", "purrr", "tibble",
#   "tidyr", "ggplot2"
# ))

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(jsonlite)
library(stringr)
library(rvest)
library(robotstxt)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

A safe alternative is to use the package name before the function:

```{r}
dplyr::glimpse(df)
readr::read_csv("data/file.csv")
jsonlite::fromJSON("data/file.json")
stringr::str_detect(x, "pattern")
rvest::read_html(url)
purrr::map_df(x, my_function)
```

# 2. Basic R Objects

## Assign a value

```{r}
x = 10
name = "Joe"
passed = TRUE
```

You can also use `<-`:

```{r}
x <- 10
```

## Vector

```{r}
numbers = c(10, 20, 30, 40)
names = c("Joe", "Bob", "Sam")
```

## Sequence

```{r}
1:10
seq(1, 10, by = 2)
```

## Basic calculations

```{r}
10 + 5
10 - 5
10 * 5
10 / 5
10^2
```

# 3. R Data Types

## Character

```{r}
x = "Miami University"
```

## Numeric

```{r}
x = 12.5
```

## Integer

```{r}
x = 12L
```

## Logical

```{r}
x = TRUE
y = FALSE
```

## Factor

Used for categorical information.

```{r}
x = factor(c("HBCU", "Non-HBCU", "HBCU"))
```

## Check a type

```{r}
class(x)
typeof(x)
```

## Convert types

```{r}
as.character(x)
as.numeric(x)
as.integer(x)
as.logical(x)
as.factor(x)
```

Important idea:

```r
# A number can represent a category.
# Example:
# 1 = HBCU
# 2 = Non-HBCU
#
# In that situation, the variable may be categorical
# even though its values are numbers.

df$hbcu_indicator = as.factor(df$hbcu_indicator)
df$carnegie_category = as.factor(df$carnegie_category)
```

# 4. Lists

## Create a list

```{r}
lst = list(
  name = "Joe",
  scores = c(90, 85, 95),
  information = list(
    age = 22,
    major = "Accountancy"
  )
)
```

## Single brackets

```{r}
lst[1]
```

Returns a list containing element 1.

## Double brackets

```{r}
lst[[1]]
```

Returns the actual element 1.

## Named element

```{r}
lst$name
```

## Nested list

```{r}
lst$information
lst$information$age
lst$information$major
```

## The key distinction

```r
lst[2]      # list containing element 2
lst[[2]]    # actual element 2
lst$name    # element named "name"
```

# 5. Data Frames / Tibbles

## Create a data frame

```{r}
df = data.frame(
  name = c("Joe", "Bob", "Sam"),
  age = c(22, 21, 23),
  major = c("Accountancy", "Finance", "Marketing")
)
```

## Create a tibble

```{r}
df = tibble::tibble(
  name = c("Joe", "Bob", "Sam"),
  age = c(22, 21, 23)
)
```

## Access a column

```{r}
df$name
df[["name"]]
df[, "name"]
```

## Access a row

```{r}
df[1, ]
```

## Access a specific cell

```{r}
df[1, 2]
```

## Access a specific column by number

```{r}
df[, 2]
```

## Multiple rows

```{r}
df[1:2, ]
```

## Multiple columns

```{r}
df[, c(1, 3)]
```

# 10. Pipes

The pipe sends the result of one operation into the next operation.

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::glimpse()
```

Example:

```{r}
df$Email |>
  stringr::str_detect("miamioh.edu") |>
  table()
```

Think:

```text
data
  ↓
operation
  ↓
operation
  ↓
answer
```

# 11. Stringr — Working with Text

## Detect a pattern

```{r}
stringr::str_detect(
  x,
  "pattern"
)
```

Example:

```{r}
emails = c(
  "joe@miamioh.edu",
  "student@gmail.com",
  "bob@miamioh.edu"
)

stringr::str_detect(
  emails,
  "miamioh.edu"
)
```

Returns TRUE/FALSE for each value.

## Count TRUE/FALSE

```{r}
stringr::str_detect(
  emails,
  "miamioh.edu"
) |>
  table()
```

## Count only matching values

```{r}
sum(
  stringr::str_detect(
    emails,
    "miamioh.edu"
  )
)
```

## Extract matching text

```{r}
stringr::str_extract(
  emails,
  "miamioh.edu"
)
```

## Replace text

```{r}
stringr::str_replace(
  emails,
  "gmail.com",
  "example.com"
)
```

## Replace all matches

```{r}
stringr::str_replace_all(
  emails,
  "gmail.com",
  "example.com"
)
```

## String length

```{r}
stringr::str_length(emails)
```

## Lowercase

```{r}
stringr::str_to_lower(emails)
```

## Uppercase

```{r}
stringr::str_to_upper(emails)
```

## Split text

```{r}
stringr::str_split(
  "Joe Sher",
  " "
)
```

# 12. Filtering Data

## Base R

```{r}
df[df$age > 21, ]
```

## dplyr

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(age > 21)
```

## Multiple conditions

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    age > 21,
    major == "Accountancy"
  )
```

## OR condition

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    major == "Accountancy" |
    major == "Finance"
  )
```

## `%in%`

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    major %in% c(
      "Accountancy",
      "Finance"
    )
  )
```

# 17. Missing Values

Check for missing values:

```{r}
is.na(df)
```

Count missing values in one variable:

```{r}
sum(is.na(df$age))
```

Filter missing:

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(age))
```

Filter non-missing:

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(age))
```

When calculating:

```{r}
mean(df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# 18. Web Scraping — Core Pattern

The basic scraping process:

```text
URL
 ↓
read_html()
 ↓
html_elements()
 ↓
html_text2() OR html_attr()
 ↓
vector/data frame
```

## Read webpage

```{r}
url = "https://example.com"

page = rvest::read_html(url)
```

## Find elements

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("h1")
```

## Extract text

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("h1") |>
  rvest::html_text2()
```

## Extract attributes

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")
```

---

# 19. CSS Selectors

## Element selector

```r
"h1"
"h2"
"h3"
"a"
"div"
"span"
"p"
```

## Class selector

If HTML has:

```html
<span class="location">
```

use:

```r
"span.location"
```

or:

```r
".location"
```

## ID selector

If HTML has:

```html
<div id="main">
```

use:

```r
"#main"
```

## Child selector

```r
"div > a > h3"
```

This means:

```text
h3
inside a
inside div
```

# 20. Scrape Links

Basic:

```{r}
links =
  "https://example.com" |>
  rvest::read_html() |>
  rvest::html_elements("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")
```

## Make relative URLs absolute

```{r}
links =
  links |>
  rvest::url_absolute(
    "https://example.com/"
  )
```

Or directly in a pipeline:

```{r}
links =
  "https://example.com" |>
  rvest::read_html() |>
  rvest::html_elements("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href") |>
  rvest::url_absolute("https://example.com/")
```

---

# 21. Exact Study-Material Pattern — Scrape Policy Links

```{r}
mu_policies =
  "https://miamioh.edu/policy-library/students/undergraduate/academic-regulations/index.html" |>
  rvest::read_html() |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    "a.news-lockup__body-link"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_attr(
    name = "href"
  ) |>
  rvest::url_absolute(
    "https://miamioh.edu/policy-library/"
  )

mu_policies
```

The key pattern is:

```text
read_html
→ html_elements
→ html_attr("href")
→ url_absolute
```

---

# 22. Exact Study-Material Pattern — Scrape Names and Locations

```{r}
page =
  rvest::read_html(
    "https://miamiredhawks.com/sports/swimming-and-diving/roster"
  )

name =
  page |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    "div > a > h3"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text2()

location =
  page |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    "span.s-person-card__content__person__location-item.flex.items-center"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text()

swim_df =
  data.frame(
    name,
    location
  )

swim_df
```

If you need to remove coaches because they are included in the scraped elements:

```{r}
swim_df =
  data.frame(
    name[1:60],
    location
  )
```

```text

 ↓

 ↓

```

# 24. Functions

## Basic function

```{r}
my_function = function(x){

  result = x * 2

  return(result)
}
```

Run it:

```{r}
my_function(5)
```

## Function with multiple arguments

```{r}
add_numbers = function(x, y){

  result = x + y

  return(result)
}

add_numbers(5, 10)
```

## Function returning a data frame

```{r}
make_df = function(x){

  df = data.frame(
    value = x
  )

  return(df)
}
```

# 25. `paste0()`

Use `paste0()` to build strings/URLs.

```{r}
x = "123"

url =
  paste0(
    "https://example.com/",
    x
  )

url
```

Multiple pieces:

```{r}
paste0(
  "https://example.com/",
  "api/",
  x,
  "?format=json"
)
```

Important:

```r
paste0("A", "B")
# "AB"
```

# 26. APIs and JSON

Basic API workflow:

```text
Build URL
 ↓
Send/read request
 ↓
JSON response
 ↓
fromJSON()
 ↓
Navigate response
 ↓
Extract information
```

## Example

```{r}
url =
  "https://api.weather.gov/points/26.142,-81.7948"

response =
  jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

response
```

Access nested information:

```{r}
response$properties
```

Specific field:

```{r}
response$properties$gridX
```

Another:

```{r}
response$properties$gridY
```

# 29. `purrr::map()`

`map()` applies a function to each element.

```{r}
numbers = c(1, 2, 3, 4)

double = function(x){
  x * 2
}

purrr::map(
  numbers,
  double
)
```

## `map_dbl()`

When each result should be a number:

```{r}
purrr::map_dbl(
  numbers,
  double
)
```

## `map_chr()`

When each result should be character:

```{r}
purrr::map_chr(
  numbers,
  as.character
)
```

## `map_df()`

When each function call returns a data frame and you want to combine rows:

```{r}
purrr::map_df(
  numbers,
  make_df
)
```

# 30. Exact Study-Material API Pattern

The study material creates a function for an IP address:

```{r}
ip_api = function(x){

  paste0(
    "http://ip-api.com/json/",
    x,
    "?fields=status,message,continent,country,countryCode,region,regionName,city,district,zip,lat,lon,timezone,currency,isp,org,as,query"
  ) |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON() ->
    response

  response |>
    as.data.frame() ->
    df

  return(df)
}
```

Then apply it to every IP:

```{r}
ip_addresses = c(
  "8.8.8.8",
  "1.1.1.1"
)

ip_df =
  purrr::map_df(
    .x = ip_addresses,
    .f = ip_api
  )

ip_df
```

For the actual study dataset:

```{r}
toxic_ips =
  readr::read_csv(
    "data/toxic_ips_oct2025.csv"
  )

ip_addresses =
  toxic_ips$IP

ip_df =
  purrr::map_df(
    .x = ip_addresses,
    .f = ip_api
)

ip_df
```

The target structure from the study material is:

```text
10 rows × 17 requested fields
```

# 31. Tidy Data

The three major tidy-data rules:

```text
1. Every variable is a column.
2. Every observation is a row.
3. Every value is a cell.
```

## Wide data

```text
country | 2020 | 2021 | 2022
```

## Long/tidy data

```text
country | year | value
```

---

# 32. `pivot_longer()`

Wide → long.

```{r}
wide_df =
  data.frame(
    country = c("USA", "Canada"),
    `2020` = c(3, 2),
    `2021` = c(4, 3),
    `2022` = c(5, 4)
  )

long_df =
  wide_df |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `2020`,
      `2021`,
      `2022`
    ),
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "value"
  )

long_df
```

---

# 33. `pivot_wider()`

Long → wide.

```{r}
wide_again =
  long_df |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = value
  )

wide_again
```

Remember:

```text
pivot_longer = wide → long
pivot_wider  = long → wide
```

---

# 34. Unit of Analysis

The unit of analysis is:

> What one row represents.

Examples:

```text
One row = one institution
→ institution

One row = one customer
→ customer

One row = one transaction
→ transaction

One row = one employee
→ employee

One row = one country
→ country
```

The key question:

```text
"What does ONE ROW represent?"
```

# 37. Joins — Know the Basic Idea

These are useful when combining datasets.

## Left join

```{r}
result =
  df1 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    df2,
    by = "id"
  )
```

## Inner join

```{r}
result =
  df1 |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    df2,
    by = "id"
  )
```

## Full join

```{r}
result =
  df1 |>
  dplyr::full_join(
    df2,
    by = "id"
  )
```

Main idea:

```text
left_join  = keep everything from left table
inner_join = keep matching rows
full_join  = keep everything from both
```

# 38. Logical Operators

You should recognize:

```r
==    # equal
!=    # not equal
>     # greater than
<     # less than
>=    # greater than or equal
<=    # less than or equal
```

AND:

```r
&
```

OR:

```r
|
```

NOT:

```r
!
```

Example:

```{r}
df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    age >= 21 &
    major == "Accountancy"
  )
```

# 40. Data Visualization / Encoding

The material emphasizes visual data encoding.

Common encodings:

```text
X-position
Y-position
Color
Size
Shape
Line type
Transparency / alpha
```

Example:

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = age,
    y = income,
    color = major,
    size = experience
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()
```

Interpretation:

```text
x       → position
y       → position
color   → category
size    → magnitude
```

---

# 41. Basic ggplot2 Patterns

Scatterplot:

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = x,
    y = y
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()
```

Bar chart:

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = category
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar()
```

Histogram:

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = value
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram()
```

Color:

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    color = category
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()
```

# 42. R vs. Spreadsheet vs. SQL

## Spreadsheet

Use when:

```text
Small/simple data
Quick manual work
Simple calculations
Quick inspection
```

## SQL

Use when:

```text
Working directly with databases
Filtering/querying tables
Joining relational tables
Aggregating database data
```

## R

Use when:

```text
Statistical analysis
Data visualization
Complex data cleaning
Automation
Reproducible analysis
Programming
Advanced analytics
```

---

# 43. Full Web-Scraping Template

Use this as a starting point for a new scraping problem:

```{r}
url =
  "https://example.com"

page =
  rvest::read_html(url)

results =
  page |>
  rvest::html_elements("CSS SELECTOR") |>
  rvest::html_text2()

results
```

For links:

```{r}
links =
  page |>
  rvest::html_elements("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")

links
```

For absolute links:

```{r}
links =
  links |>
  rvest::url_absolute(url)

links
```

# 44. Full API Template

```{r}
url =
  "https://example.com/api"

response =
  jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

dplyr::glimpse(response)
```

Then inspect nested information:

```{r}
names(response)
```

```{r}
response$properties
```

```{r}
response$properties$value
```

---

# 45. Full API + Function + map_df Template

```{r}
api_function = function(x){

  url =
    paste0(
      "https://example.com/api/",
      x
    )

  response =
    jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

  df =
    as.data.frame(response)

  return(df)
}

results =
  purrr::map_df(
    items,
    api_function
)
```

This is one of the most important templates in the entire study guide.

---

# 46. Full CSV → API → Data Frame Template

```{r}
input =
  readr::read_csv(
    "data/input.csv"
  )

items =
  input$IP

api_function = function(x){

  url =
    paste0(
      "http://ip-api.com/json/",
      x
    )

  response =
    jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

  response |>
    as.data.frame()
}

output =
  purrr::map_df(
    items,
    api_function
)

output
```

# 47. Quick Exam Recognition Guide

```text
lst[2]
→ list containing element 2

lst[[2]]
→ element 2 itself

df[500, ]
→ row 500

nrow(df)
→ observations

ncol(df)
→ variables

glimpse(df)
→ structure/overview

str_detect()
→ find whether text contains a pattern

fromJSON()
→ JSON into R

read_csv()
→ CSV into R

read_html()
→ webpage into R

html_elements()
→ find HTML elements

html_text2()
→ extract text

html_attr("href")
→ extract links

url_absolute()
→ make URL complete

paths_allowed()
→ check robots.txt

function(x)
→ create a function

map()
→ apply function repeatedly

map_df()
→ apply + combine into data frame

pivot_longer()
→ wide to long

pivot_wider()
→ long to wide

as.factor()
→ categorical/factor

unit of analysis
→ what one row represents

color
→ visual encoding

x/y
→ positional encoding
```

# Final Mental Model

When you encounter a new problem, ask:

```text
1. What kind of data is this?
        ↓
2. How do I import it?
        ↓
3. What does one row represent?
        ↓
4. What are the variable types?
        ↓
5. How do I inspect it?
        ↓
6. Do I need to filter/select/mutate?
        ↓
7. Is this text/string manipulation?
        ↓
8. Is this a webpage?
        ↓
9. Is this an API?
        ↓
10. Is the response JSON/nested?
        ↓
11. Do I need a function?
        ↓
12. Do I need map/map_df?
        ↓
13. Is the resulting data tidy?
        ↓
14. How would I visualize/encode it?
```

This is the **core R workflow** represented by the material you provided.
